charts.title: Every probe, every store
charts.description: All 30 answers are retained, including wrong values and evidence failures. Q01–Q10 map to the expandable question table below.

charts.title: Answer versus abstention decisions
charts.description: Rows are the gold answerability; columns are the model's decision. Answering an answerable question is not necessarily correct—the exact-value plots score that separately.

charts.title: Fresh run versus the previous smoke
charts.description: Same fixture and nominal model/effort; this run rebuilds the stores and resamples readers. Changes can come from either builder or reader stochasticity. Two runs do not establish a trend or a significant improvement.

charts.title: Retrieval budget use for every probe
charts.description: Every returned UTF-8 byte counts, including paths, snippets, errors and repeated reads. This is a byte budget, not a model-token cap. Unused budget does not imply that enough relevant evidence was retrieved.

charts.title: Which tools did the reader use?
charts.description: Host list/read/search actions only. The final answer and provider completions are not counted as retrieval actions. More tool calls alone are not evidence of better retrieval.

charts.title: Reader call depth
charts.description: The sixth completion is reserved for an answer or unknown. A response at the cap may still be incomplete. Calls are measured independently of the retrieved-byte budget.

charts.title: Observed reader latency
charts.description: Dots are the ten probes; horizontal lines are medians. The three arm processes run concurrently. Values include repeated Codex startup/inference and local tool handling, and are not a controlled serial latency benchmark.

charts.title: Reader input and cache accounting
charts.description: Cached input is a subset of total input, never added twice. Counts include instructions, repeated history and retrieved material across every completion. Token totals are not USD prices.

charts.title: Reader generation volume
charts.description: Reported output tokens across ten probes. Separately reported reasoning tokens are not added to this total. The CLI's output-token target is advisory; the enforced controls are calls, time and retrieval bytes.

charts.title: Input footprint by question
charts.description: Input is summed over all reader completions for that probe, including cache hits. High input can reflect repeated protocol overhead rather than more unique context read.

charts.title: Measured work by phase
charts.description: Within-arm builder and reader operation durations are summed. Setup/report overhead is excluded. Do not sum all three bars to estimate elapsed time: the arms run concurrently.

charts.title: Fresh build latency per window
charts.description: All six snapshots were built fresh. S3 includes real model maintenance; S0 and S1 are deterministic local writers. The log axis keeps small local fold times visible without implying they have equal cost.

charts.title: S3 builder token work
charts.description: Each bar aggregates the Codex completions required for one successful fold. Deterministic S0/S1 writers make no builder model calls. These are new builds, not reused snapshots.

charts.title: Reader-visible store growth
charts.description: Measured from the exact reader-visible text export for each committed SHA. Git objects, evaluator ledgers, builder instructions and transient source mounts are excluded. Size alone is not semantic retention.

charts.title: Reader-visible file count
charts.description: Measured from the exact reader-visible text export for each committed SHA. Git objects, evaluator ledgers, builder instructions and transient source mounts are excluded. Size alone is not semantic retention.

charts.title: Observed quality versus input footprint
charts.description: One point per store on one ten-probe workload. This is not a cost-optimal frontier: USD prices, independent build repetitions and held-out measurements are absent.

charts.title: Infrastructure verification
